chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abdurrahman ibn Maslama al-Jareeri, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, people blame us and say: From where is the truthful (call) distinguished from the false one when they both occur?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'With what do you answer them?' I said: 'We answer them with nothing.' He said: 'Say to them: He who has believed in them before they occur will know which of them is true when they occur.'

Say: 'Are there any of your partners who guide to the truth?' Say: 'Allah guides to the truth.' So, is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not go aright unless he is guided? What then is the matter with you; how do you judge?'
ai.seo_question: How do believers distinguish true prophetic signs from false ones according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the recognition of the Mahdi and other eschatological signs relies on the pre-existing faith of the believers, who will acknowledge their truth before their manifestation. He supports this by citing Surah Yunus (10:71) to contrast Allah’s guidance with that of false deities, arguing that the true guide is inherently more worthy of following than those who merely wait to be guided. This hadith underscores the Shia principle that certainty in the Imam’s identity is rooted in theological conviction rather than mere observation of events.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (32) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan at-Taymali from his father from Muhammad bin Khalid from Tha’lba bin Maymoon that Abdurrahman bin Maslama al-Jareeri had said: “I said to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as): “Some people blame us and say that how the truthful call is distinguished from the false one when they both occur.”
He said: “With what do you answer them?” I said: “With nothing.” He said: “Say to them: He, who has believed in them before they occur, will know which of them is true and which is false.
Allah has said, ‘Is He then Who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who himself does not go aright unless he is guided? What then is the matter with you; how do you judge?’”
